findings.summary: The layer stack is a run of one-word lines, so the order and the pairing of layer to tool are unclear.
findings.evidence:
IP on interface
ip
Route
gateway
DNS
dig
Port
ss, curl
Firewall
allows it
findings.fix: Replace the lines with a table (Layer | Check | Tool) or a top-to-bottom diagram, and show the bottom-up debug order as numbered steps.

findings.summary: The debug order in section 3 leaves out the firewall layer, which section 1 lists as the last layer to check.
findings.evidence: Section 1 ends with "Firewall allows it" and "Debug bottom-up in that order". Section 3 ends at "curl -v service answers?" and has no firewall step.
findings.fix: Add a final firewall step to the ordered checklist, for example "ufw status / security group: is the port allowed?".

findings.summary: One table row packs three unrelated flags and three ideas into a single bullet.
findings.fix: Split it into three rows: -X sets the method, -H adds a header, -d sends the body.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "production", "running").
findings.evidence: scp -p vs -P, running ss without sudo (no process names shown), and using curl -k in production. Use nc -zv host port to test whether a TCP port is open.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The term 'security group' is used as a firewall layer, but no page ever defines it.
findings.evidence: Timeout | Firewall or security group drops packets, or bad route; ufw allow 8080 alone: cloud security group or router still blocks
findings.fix: Add one line on page 5: a security group is the cloud provider's firewall in front of the instance, managed outside the host, so it must also allow the port.

findings.summary: The wording is ambiguous: "unreachable either way" does not say that a loopback bind blocks remote clients whatever the firewall allows.
findings.fix: Reword to "Bound to 127.0.0.1: remote clients cannot connect even if the firewall allows the port".

findings.summary: The timeout check points to a command that does not test for a firewall drop.
findings.evidence: Timeout | Firewall or security group drops packets, or bad route | ip route get IP
findings.fix: Add a firewall check next to the route check, for example "sudo ufw status; check the security group".

findings.summary: The reachability code block has no one-line note saying what each command is for, unlike the other tables on the page.
findings.evidence:
ping -c 4 host
nc -zv host port
curl -v URL
curl -sI URL
curl -w '%{http_code}' -o /dev/null -s URL
findings.fix: Turn it into a Command | Answers table, or add a short comment to each line.
